# Hugh Carrow

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen in Volume 1, turning nineteen during Volume 2, and twenty-two by Volume 5.  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c19 P40](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0040), [v1 c25 P61](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0061)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive
- **Rank:** Medical Doctor (M.D.)  <sub>[v1 c28 P35](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0035), [v1 c36 P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley (Carrow orchard across the Lake of Glassy Waters / St. Brendan's Island)  <sub>[v1 c2 P2](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0002), [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c17 P24](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0024)</sub>
- **Role:** Medical doctor at Seven Gulls; former schoolteacher at Pale Sands and journalist at the Daily News.  <sub>[v1 c24 P1](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0001), [v1 c28 P35](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0035), [v1 c31 P0](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0000), [v1 c36 P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)</sub>
- **Titles:** Dr. Carrow  <sub>[v1 c36 P35](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0035)</sub>; Captain of the Freshman football team  <sub>[v1 c24 P6](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0006)</sub>; Medalist / Winner of the Cooper Prize  <sub>[v1 c30 P24](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0024), [v1 c36 P3](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0003)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Hughie  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>

## Appearance

Hugh is a tall, handsome youth with wavy chestnut hair, mischievous light-brown (hazel) eyes, and a broad-shouldered, athletic build. He has a firm, handsome chin and a lively, expressive face that often bears a mocking or friendly grin. Following a severe bout of typhoid fever, he appeared pale and thin for a time, but he retains a tall, manly posture as he matures into adulthood.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c30 P37](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0037), [v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037)_

## Personality

Hugh is lively, mischievous, and confident, with a keen sense of humor and a competitive drive. Though prone to teasing and occasional daring pranks in his early school days, he is deeply honorable, brave, and generous at heart, willing to admit his mistakes and make sacrifices for others. As he grows, he demonstrates a serious, dedicated work ethic toward his studies and medical vocation, maintaining high ideals while remaining warm, cheerful, and steadfastly loyal in his affections.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c27 P14](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0014), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038)_

## History

Hugh Carrow grows up in Brierley and spends three years of his childhood in Alberta with his father. Returning to Brierley School at fourteen, he initially teases Nell Harcourt by calling her 'Carrots', prompting her to break a slate over his head, an incident for which he immediately apologizes. Though Nell holds a grudge, Hugh competes with her academically at school and later at Regent's Academy. After working as a teacher at Pale Sands and a journalist at the Daily News to fund his education, he attends Wexcombe College, where he becomes captain of the Freshman football team, joins the Lambda Theta fraternity, and earns High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize. Upon learning Nell wishes to teach in Brierley to stay near her foster-mother, Hugh unselfishly withdraws his own application for the Brierley school so she can have it, taking the Pale Sands position instead. Over time, his early romantic overtures are rejected by Nell, leading to a period of distant friendship while rumor links him to Rowena Calder. However, after surviving a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever and completing his medical degree, Hugh's steadfast love for Nell is finally reciprocated. Upon taking over his great-uncle Dr. David Carrow's practice in Seven Gulls, Hugh leases a small white house by the harbour shore. He and Nell are married in the apple orchard at Grey Shutters and settle in Seven Gulls, where they later welcome their son, James Obed (Little Kit).

## Background by volume

- Son of John Carrow, residing at the ancient Carrow orchard across the Lake of Glassy Waters  <sub>[v1 c17 P24](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0024), [v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037)</sub>
- Lived in Alberta for three years during childhood while his father was ill  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- Great-nephew of Dr. David Carrow of Glen St. Agnes  <sub>[v1 c36 P15](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0015)</sub>
- Attended Brierley School, Regent's Academy in Port Marlow, and Wexcombe College  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c17 P37](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0037), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011)</sub>
- Survived a life-threatening case of typhoid fever during his youth  <sub>[v1 c23 P30](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0030)</sub>

## Quotes

> Mr. Pidgeon, the blame belongs to me because I provoked her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042)</sub>

> Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair. Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.  <sub>[v1 c15 P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)</sub>

> I’m going to have my own way about my own house, I can tell you.  <sub>[v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025)</sub>

> For a period back then, after you informed me that you could never care for me, Nell, nothing held much significance for me. There was no other person—for me, there could never be anyone but you. My love for you has endured from the moment you shattered your slate across my head at school.  <sub>[v1 c28 P29](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0029)</sub>
